doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Future plans and working steadily
summary: Upcoming festivals, work for Louis Bellson, an album with Jane Jarvis, and the downside of steady work.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: What’s in the future for you guys? Any recording projects coming up?
Right now I seem to be becalmed actually.
Well I saw you, we worked at South Carolina Jazz Festival a couple of months ago down in Columbia. And we had a little party for Clark Terry, his 75th birthday. So that was fun.

Oh, yeah, we’ll be doing some jazz festivals and things like that. Recording comes and goes. I just did some things for Louis Bellson, who maintains a big band sometimes. And the trick is to get somebody to pay for a date for a big band. So that was different, you know it was fun to do and all that.
Did you do something with Jane Jarvis fairly recently?

I made an album with her several years ago, with Monty Budwig and Jake Hanna. That was fun. And we did it in a little small studio. Yeah I’d forgotten about that, that was nice. Those things come and go, it’s hard to predict. I had forgotten about, from being steadily employed all those years, you know. But now you can’t predict what’s happening. I mean there’s things coming up, I’ve got something in Phoenix next year and something with Jane Jarvis in Tampa this year in November. But somehow it fills itself in, doesn’t it? I mean I couldn’t really say what’s happening except on certain long term things.

Yeah, I was looking the other day, because we worked every day for so long it was funny not to show up someplace every day, until you get used to it. And I’m looking, the only way I can keep track is the American Express book calendar they send you once a year and you can write down where you’re supposed to be. And as I looked through my book it’s slowly getting busier and busier. It’s slow but—
You see working steady is a two-edged sword. Because they say don’t bother, call somebody else because he’s busy.
Word gets out that you can’t do it.
It happens, yeah. But the nice part is that you know where your next meal’s coming from, too.
